summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a thrombosed left upper extremity AV graft, preventing dialysis. She also reported persistent abdominal nodules at insulin injection sites and chronic urinary symptoms. Imaging confirmed bladder wall enhancement suggestive of infection and a non-specific lytic lesion in L1, but no abscesses or calciphylaxis. The AV graft was successfully recanalized via thrombectomy. Wound culture from a prior breast biopsy grew pan-sensitive E. coli and Proteus, treated with targeted IV ceftazidime. Urine culture was contaminated, but symptoms improved with empiric antibiotics. She completed one dialysis session during admission and was transitioned to outpatient IV antibiotic administration post-dialysis. Discharged home with services, on a plan for continued dialysis, wound care, and close follow-up for unresolved abdominal nodules and repeat urine testing if symptoms persist.
